key_insight: Ill-posed questions leave a geometric signature in LLM hidden states, and that topology can be used to both detect ambiguity and steer answers toward clarification or abstention.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a model-agnostic, layerwise diagnostic for hard prompts that can improve reliability in deployed LLM systems by triggering safer, source-aware responses.
method: Represent prompt-token hidden states at each transformer layer as a point cloud.
Compute 0D persistent homology and summarize each layer with mean finite lifetime, normalized lifetime entropy, and largest-lifetime concentration.
Concatenate layerwise topology descriptors and use nearest topological neighbors to build activation steering interventions.
evidence_signal: Across AmbigQA, SituatedQA, and CLAMBER, topology features improved average ill-posedness classification accuracy from 67.4% to 78.9%, 79.9% to 88.5%, and 57.6% to 69.6%, while steering raised total acceptable responses from 61.4% to 70.6% and grounded acceptable responses from 11.9% to 16.4%.
watch_item: The approach depends on extracting and intervening in internal activations, so portability, compute cost, and behavior consistency across model families and prompt domains may be limited.
paper_title: The Topology of Ill-Posed Questions: Persistent Homology for Detection and Steering in LLMs
